definition: a written or printed work made up of pages bound together
hook: Book is named after a tree, not a story.
modernAnchor: We still call it a book on a screen with no pages and no wood anywhere near it.
journey: Early Germanic peoples carved runes into thin wooden tablets to keep records and send messages.
Beech wood was common and easy to inscribe, so Old English speakers called these tablets boc, beech.
As writing shifted to parchment and then paper, English kept the old name for whatever the words sat on.
Screens replaced pages for many readers, and the word survived that too, still tied to a tree it left behind.
